learningBasics.seo: Guided Meditation for Beginners: Free Mindfulness Sessions
learningBasics.desc: Guided meditation for beginners: never meditated? Follow {n} free mindfulness sessions of {min} to {max} minutes, step by step. No ads, no account, works offline.
learningBasics.h1: Free guided meditation for beginners, step by step
intro: Guided meditation for beginners starts here, if you have never meditated or want to rebuild your practice on solid ground. These {n} short sessions, each one a guided mindfulness meditation, cover the essentials one step at a time. You start with a body scan and steady your attention on the breath. Then you learn to tell sensations, emotions and thoughts apart, and to watch thoughts go by. A mindful eating meditation, the five senses and meditating with your eyes open come next. The last session is your first silent meditation.

These short mindfulness sessions last between {min} and {max} minutes and are all designed for beginners. You can follow them in order or pick the theme that speaks to you today. Like everything in MeditaDream, they are free, need no account and play offline once downloaded.
faq: How long should a beginner meditate?

There is no fixed rule. The sessions in this category last from {min} to {max} minutes, which is a comfortable range when you are starting out. A short session done regularly is usually easier to keep up than a long one you postpone.
Do I need any experience or equipment?
No. Each session explains what to do as you go, and all you need is a quiet place to sit or lie down and your phone. Headphones can help you stay focused, but they are not required.
In what order should I follow the sessions?

You can follow them in the order they appear, starting with the body scan and the breath, then moving on to thoughts and the senses. Your first silent meditation makes a natural final step once the other sessions feel familiar.
Is there a completely free meditation app for beginners?
Yes. MeditaDream is 100% free: no subscription, no trial, no ads and no account. All {n} guided meditations for beginners are included, along with the rest of the library.
What is the best guided meditation for beginners?

The best one is the one you will actually do, so start small. First Meditation is a good way in: in six minutes, it explains what meditating is, then lets you practice noticing where your attention goes and bringing it back. Once that feels comfortable, move on to the body scan or the breath session.
Is there a 5-minute meditation for beginners?

Yes, two sessions fit into a short break. Your First Silent Meditation lasts 5 minutes and includes real silences, which are part of the practice. First Meditation lasts 6 minutes and shows you what to do with your attention. Either one is enough for a first day, and you can repeat it as often as you like.
How do I learn to meditate for free?

The simplest way is to start with a guided session: a voice tells you what to notice, so you learn by doing. The {n} sessions listed on this page are free in the app, with no trial and no account. Each one teaches a single skill, such as feeling the body, following the breath or watching thoughts pass. Repeat a session until it feels familiar, then move to the next.

guide.h2: How to start meditating: your first week
p: Day one, try the five-minute silent meditation to see how it feels to simply sit. Days two and three, follow the body scan. Days four and five, work with the breath. Days six and seven, add two mindfulness exercises: the observing thoughts meditation and mindful eating.
At the end of the week, pick the session you enjoyed most and keep it as your anchor. A short daily habit beats a long session you keep putting off.

For absolute beginners, this is the easiest meditation program to start with: one short session a day, for seven days. When you want a longer plan, the blog lays out a free meditation course for beginners over four weeks.

guide.h2: What does meditation for beginners feel like?
p: In a guided mindfulness meditation, a calm voice tells you what to notice, one step at a time. You sit or lie down, close your eyes if you like, and follow along. There is nothing to get right. Wondering how to meditate in bed? The body scan works well lying down.
Your mind will wander, often within seconds. That is not failure. Noticing it and coming back is the exercise itself.

guide.h2: Guided mindfulness meditation: one anchor at a time
p: Mindfulness means paying attention, on purpose, to what is happening right now, without judging it. You do not have to empty your mind: in guided mindfulness meditation, you pick one anchor and come back to it each time you drift.

The sessions here use different anchors: the body in the body scan, the breath in mindful breathing, then thoughts, the five senses and a single bite of food. One simple thing at a time, a few minutes a day: that is all it takes when you are starting out. Meditation for beginners is easiest at home, in the same quiet spot each day: a chair, a cushion or the edge of your bed is enough.

guide.h2: Free, with no catch
p: Many apps lock beginner courses behind a trial or a subscription. Here, every session is free, with no account and no ads. Download a session once and it plays offline, wherever you are.

fourMin.seo: Quick Meditation for Anxiety: {n} Guided Sessions Under 5 Min
fourMin.desc: Quick meditation for anxiety: {n} guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes. A 5-minute meditation for anxiety, with time to spare. Free, no ads, works offline.
fourMin.h1: Quick meditation for anxiety: calm the mind in 3 or 4 minutes
intro: A quick meditation for anxiety helps when you only have a few minutes. These eleven short sessions are built for those moments: each one fits where a 5-minute meditation for anxiety would, with a minute or two to spare. Use one when everything moves too fast, after an argument, before a challenge or after bad news. Others help when self motivation runs low, or when you feel watched or judged. Some simply help you relax very quickly, revisit a happy memory or practice precise gratitude. Another gives you a small refuge of your own.

Whether you need a guided meditation for anxiety, a stress break or a gentle pause, each session lasts three to four minutes and suits beginners. They are easy to slip into a coffee break, a commute or the moment just before a meeting. Keep a few favorites close at hand: once downloaded, they work without a connection, wherever you happen to be.
faq: Can a 4-minute meditation really make a difference?

A few minutes is enough to pause, notice your breath and step back from what is happening. These sessions are not meant to replace a longer practice, but they give you a simple way to reset in the middle of a busy day.
When is the best time for a short meditation?

Whenever you need a pause: between two tasks, before a hard conversation, on the bus or after work. With eyes open at your desk, it also makes a discreet mindfulness meditation at work. Several sessions are named after a specific situation, so you can pick the one that fits.
Do I need to be experienced?
No. All eleven sessions are designed for beginners and guide you step by step. You can keep your eyes open for some of them, which makes them easy to use almost anywhere.
Is a 5-minute meditation for anxiety enough?
For a daily habit, yes. A short meditation for anxiety done every day is easier to keep than a long one you postpone. These sessions last three to four minutes, and you can chain them.
Is there a free guided meditation for anxiety I can start right now?

Yes. All eleven sessions are free, with no account, no subscription and no ads. Install MeditaDream, open the 4 Minutes category and press play: the shortest sessions take three minutes. Once a session is downloaded, it plays anywhere, even in airplane mode.
How do you calm your mind from anxiety in a few minutes?

Give your attention something concrete. Keep your eyes open and choose one object: notice its color and one detail. Feel your feet on the floor, find one sound, then let the air come in and flow out on its own. That is what “When Everything Moves Too Fast” guides you through in four minutes. These sessions support well-being and never replace a health professional.

guide.h2: Quick meditation for anxiety: 5 minutes or 10, build your own
p: Each session lasts three or four minutes. The shortest make a 3-minute meditation you can fit between two tasks. Play one as a 5-minute morning meditation before you check your phone. Chain two or three and you have your own 10-minute meditation for anxiety.
They work with your eyes open, at your desk, on a bus or just before a meeting.

guide.h2: How to relieve anxiety quickly: a session for each moment
p: Stress and rush: “When Everything Moves Too Fast” (4 min) keeps your eyes open on an object and the floor until your breath settles; “Relax Very Quickly” (3 min) releases the body area by area, from forehead to feet.

Before or after a hard moment: “Finding Your Confidence Before a Challenge” (4 min) separates what depends on you from what does not. Here is how to calm down quickly after a clash: “Calming Down After an Argument” (3 min) loosens what tightened. “After Receiving Bad News” (4 min) brings you back to what is true right here, right now.

When your morale dips: “When You Lack Motivation” (3 min) keeps only the first concrete step. “When You Feel Like Giving Up” (3 min) tells passing tiredness apart from a real decision. Wondering how to calm social anxiety before a meeting? “When You Feel Watched or Judged” (4 min) sorts what you actually know from what you imagine.

Need a gentle pause, or a 5-minute guided visualization meditation? Try “Your Instant Refuge” (4 min), a short safe place visualization where worries can wait. “A Happy Memory Through Three Senses” (4 min) warms up the present, and “Precise Gratitude” (3 min) closes the day.

guide.h2: Try it now: a 3-minute meditation for a tense moment
p: No time to open the app? Here is the idea in four moves, eyes open. One: stop, and rest your eyes on a single object; notice its color and one detail. Two: feel your feet on the floor and the chair holding your weight. Three: find one sound and follow it for a few breaths, letting the air come and go on its own. Four: name the next small thing you will do, and only that one.
This micro meditation takes about three minutes. It will not solve what worries you, but it gives your attention a steady place to stand while the wave passes.

calm.seo: Sleep Meditation: {n} Guided Bedtime Sessions for Deep Sleep
calm.desc: Sleep meditation that works in bed, lights off: {n} guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes, from bedtime meditation to deep relaxation. Free, no ads, offline.
calm.h1: Guided deep sleep meditation and relaxation
intro: Body, Calm & Sleep gathers {n} sessions to slow down and let go. Some are sleep meditations made for the end of the day. A bedtime meditation such as Sleep Journey or Drifting into Sleep lets you slide into sleep, with no wake-up at the end. Others work with breath and the body, such as Breathing with the Whole Body, The Luminous Breath or The Body Under a Waterfall. You will also find sessions on the seven chakras, a session to prepare for lucid dreaming and a session to calm your mind before creative work.

Sessions run from {min} to {max} minutes and are marked as intermediate, with a slow voice and generous pauses. Lie down comfortably, lower the lights and let the voice guide you. Once downloaded, they play offline, so you can switch your phone to airplane mode and listen in bed without any interruption.
faq: Which session should I choose to fall asleep?

Sleep Journey and Drifting into Sleep are designed for bedtime. They gradually release effort and end without a wake-up, so you can simply let sleep come. Chakra Reset, with its long restful pauses, is another gentle option for the evening.
Can I listen in bed without a connection?
Yes. Once a session is downloaded, it plays offline, so you can put your phone in airplane mode at night. The app has no ads, so nothing will interrupt the session.
Is sleep meditation for beginners too?

Yes. These sessions are marked as intermediate and last {min} to {max} minutes, but falling asleep asks for no skill. If you are new to meditation, Learning Basics or the four-minute sessions make an easy start.
What is the best free guided sleep meditation?
Start with Drifting into Sleep, a 16-minute session made for falling asleep. It is free, like everything in MeditaDream, with no account and no ads, and it plays offline.
Is this sleep hypnosis?

Not exactly. Sleep hypnosis relies on suggestion, while these sessions guide the breath and the body with a slow voice. The effect can feel close: Drifting into Sleep is a hypnotic sleep meditation, with long pauses and no wake-up. If you usually play free sleep hypnosis tracks, give it a try tonight.
Is there a guided meditation for sleep and anxiety?

When racing thoughts keep you up, choose a sleep meditation that starts with the body rather than the thoughts. Breathing with the Whole Body (13 min) gives your attention one simple thing to follow. Then Drifting into Sleep lets every effort go, with no wake-up at the end. These sessions support well-being and never replace a health professional.
What to do when you can’t sleep?

Stop trying to sleep, which tends to keep you awake, and give your mind an easy task instead. Play Sleep Journey with the phone face down and follow the voice from your feet upward, one area at a time. If you are still awake at the end, stay with the feeling of weight on the mattress. Sleep comes more easily when you are not chasing it.

guide.h2: Night meditation for sleep: a simple bedtime routine
p: Here is how to meditate for sleep: get into bed, dim the lights and start a session. Put the phone face down beside you. There is nothing to do except listen.
Falling asleep before the end is fine. That is what the session is for.

Keep the same session for a week and it becomes part of your sleep routine: its first words turn into a signal that the day is over. For the rest of the evening, the blog has a bedtime routine for adults that takes 15 minutes.

guide.h2: Which sleep meditation to pick tonight
p: To drift off quickly, try Drifting into Sleep, a gentle 16-minute session. If you are after a guided meditation for deep sleep, Sleep Journey is the long one: 27 minutes of slow wind-down, with nothing to remember at the end.
If your body still feels tense, start with Breathing with the Whole Body. If you like to dream, Lucid Dream Preparation takes you all the way to sleep.

guide.h2: Relaxation for sleep: let the body go first
p: Some nights the mind is ready for sleep and the body is not. On those nights, take it in two steps. Begin with a body session: Breathing with the Whole Body (13 min) lets you feel the breath move far beyond the chest, and The Body Under a Waterfall (15 min) pours imagined water over your head, shoulders and back. Both end with your eyes open, so follow either one with Drifting into Sleep or Sleep Journey, which have no wake-up.

This two-step guided meditation for sleep and relaxation takes half an hour or a little more. If you have practiced yoga nidra for sleep, the slow tour of the body in Sleep Journey will feel familiar.

guide.h2: Works offline, in bed
p: MeditaDream is a guided sleep meditation app you can use with your phone in airplane mode: download a session once and it plays without a connection. On quieter nights, the app also has sleep sounds such as rain or ocean waves, with a fade-out timer.

emotionalGrowth.seo: Free Self-Compassion Meditation for Self-Love and Gratitude
emotionalGrowth.desc: Self-compassion meditation for a kinder inner voice: {n} guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes on self-love, gratitude and forgiveness. Free, no ads.
intro: Emotional Growth offers {n} sessions of self-compassion and self-love meditation, to cultivate kindness toward yourself and an open heart. You can practice daily gratitude starting from the body, look for real reasons to love yourself, open your heart, explore what forgiving might mean without forgetting, and let go of comparison. Other sessions help you welcome a difficult emotion with curiosity, picture your growth along an old railway, or send wishes of peace and happiness to yourself and to others. Two short, practical sessions round things out: one helps you make a decision step by step, the other is about building self-confidence on evidence, one small action at a time.

Sessions last {min} to {max} minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit anyone looking for more self-kindness, and a softer eye on others, at their own pace. Short sessions such as Compassion Meditation, seven minutes, are an easy way in, while the longer ones give you more time to stay with what you feel.
faq: What is a compassion meditation?

It is close to a guided loving kindness meditation. You send wishes of peace, safety and happiness, first to yourself, then to others. The Compassion Meditation in this category lasts 7 minutes and is a simple way to try it.
Do I have to forgive someone during the forgiveness session?

No. Forgiving Without Forgetting is a guided forgiveness meditation, with no pressure to forgive. It invites you to explore what forgiveness might mean for you, then to decide for yourself whether to set something down or keep it, while holding on to what you have learned.
How often should I practice gratitude?
The Daily Gratitude session is short enough to be repeated often. You might like to use it in the evening, but the best rhythm is the one you can keep without forcing yourself.
What is a good self love meditation for beginners?
Developing Self-love is a 15-minute guided session made for beginners. Follow it with Releasing Comparison when you are ready.
What is mindful self-compassion?

It means noticing a hard moment with mindfulness, then answering it with the kindness you would offer a friend. Developing Self-love and Welcoming a Difficult Emotion train both gestures, at a gentle pace.
Is there a meditation for self-esteem here?

Yes, three sessions work on it from different sides. Developing Self-love asks you to find something real to appreciate in yourself. Releasing Comparison loosens the habit of measuring yourself against others. Building Self-Confidence Through Evidence and Action has you recall what you have already managed, then choose one small step. None of them asks you to repeat flattering phrases: they start from facts.

guide.h2: Self love meditation, one small step at a time
p: These sessions help you speak to yourself more gently, a first step toward self-acceptance. You learn to welcome an emotion, compare yourself less and notice what is already good.
Self love here is not a big statement. Like all self love practices, it is a habit you build, a few minutes at a time.

Wondering how to practice self-love without forcing it? Start with something true: one quality you can actually point to, as Developing Self-love invites you to do. What grows from there is a kind of inner compassion, the patience you would have for a friend, turned toward yourself.

guide.h2: Which self-compassion meditation fits what you need today?
p: To begin, Developing Self-love, 15 minutes. For a heavy feeling, Welcoming a Difficult Emotion. Short on time? Compassion Meditation lasts seven minutes. For a self forgiveness meditation, Forgiving Yourself waits in the Shadow & Well-being category.

Used this way, the sessions double as short self-compassion exercises you can return to on a hard day. For the classic method behind Compassion Meditation, the blog explains loving-kindness meditation step by step.

guide.h2: Gratitude meditation: a small museum of your day
p: Daily Gratitude is a 14-minute guided gratitude meditation that walks you through a small museum of your day. Each room holds an ordinary moment you could have forgotten: the first sip of a drink, a sound, something that simply worked, a face, one thing your body did for you. You do not have to feel happy, only to notice.
Play it in the evening, while the day is still fresh, or whenever it has felt heavy. If you like to write, one line in the gratitude journal afterward is enough to hold on to it.

shadow.seo: Shadow Work Meditation and Inner Child: {n} Free Sessions
shadow.desc: Shadow work meditation, the gentle way: {n} guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes for your inner child, everyday fears and Ho’oponopono. Free, no ads.
shadow.h1: Guided shadow work meditation: meet your shadow gently
intro: Shadow & Well-being is a set of shadow work meditations: it invites you to meet, with care, what you usually turn away from. The Shadow Work session helps you understand what a difficult part of yourself is trying to protect. An inner child meditation reconnects you with play and safety, and another session guides you through forgiving yourself. A Ho’oponopono meditation lets you repeat the four phrases of reconciliation with your breath. Short sessions also look at common fears: abandonment, failure, judgment and the dark.

Sessions last 7 to 21 minutes and are marked as intermediate. Each one moves gently, keeps an anchor in the body and lets you stop whenever you need to. They are meant for relaxation and self-exploration, not as a substitute for professional support.
faq: What is shadow work?

Shadow work means turning toward the parts of yourself you tend to avoid, such as fears, old reactions or feelings you would rather not see. In this category, it is done gently, with the aim of understanding rather than judging.
What is Ho’oponopono?

Ho’oponopono is a Hawaiian practice built around four short phrases of reconciliation. The Ho’oponopono meaning is often given as “to make right.” In Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono, you repeat the phrases with your breath for about 15 minutes, without forcing anything. The four phrases, often called the Ho’oponopono prayer, are “I’m sorry,” “Please forgive me,” “Thank you” and “I love you.”
What if a session brings up something difficult?

You can pause or stop at any time. The sessions keep you connected to your body and move at a gentle pace. If difficult feelings persist, talking to someone you trust or to a professional is always a good idea.
What is shadow work meditation?
A guided practice for meeting the parts of yourself you usually hide or push away, with kindness. Start with a short session on a single fear.
How do I start shadow work as a beginner?

Start small and specific. Pick one everyday fear, not your whole past: Fear of Judgment lasts 7 minutes and Fear of Failure 10. Keep one hand on your chest or belly as an anchor, and stop when you have had enough. After a few sessions, move on to Shadow Work, which looks at a difficult part of you and what it protects.
Is shadow work dangerous?

Done gently, it is uncomfortable more often than dangerous: you look at feelings you usually avoid, and that can stir things up. These sessions keep an anchor in the body, move slowly and let you stop at any time. They are made for relaxation and self-exploration. If you are going through a very hard period, do this kind of work with a professional, not alone.

guide.h2: Shadow work meditation, gently
p: Your shadow, sometimes called the shadow self, is what you would rather not see in yourself: a fear, anger, an old hurt. Meditation helps you look at this inner shadow with kindness, at your own pace.
You can always stop. Go only as far as feels right today. The blog explains how to do shadow work in more depth.
The aim is not to get rid of that part of you but to know it well enough that it stops running the show. In Jungian psychology, this is called shadow integration.

guide.h2: Shadow work exercises: where to start
p: The sessions on fears are short, seven to thirteen minutes: Fear of Judgment, Fear of Failure. To go further, try Shadow Work. If you wonder how to process guilt, Forgiving Yourself is a gentle self forgiveness meditation.

guide.h2: Fear of failure, fear of abandonment: one meditation for each fear
p: Four short sessions each take a single fear. Fear of Failure helps you separate “I failed” from “I am a failure.” Fear of Abandonment keeps one hand resting on your body as an anchor while the feeling comes up. Fear of Judgment loosens the sense of being watched, and Fear of the Dark lets you get used to darkness little by little.

None of them tries to argue the fear away. You stay close to it for a few minutes, at a distance you choose. Releasing Fear, 16 minutes, goes one step further and looks at what an old fear has been guarding.

sacred.seo: Sacred Places: {n} Free Guided Nature Meditations, {min}–{max} Min
sacred.desc: Meditate in sacred places, from the Bodhi tree to Stonehenge and the northern lights: {n} guided nature meditations of {min} to {max} minutes. Free, offline.
sacred.h1: Guided nature meditation in sacred places
intro: Sacred Places takes you to seven remarkable settings, each one a guided nature meditation. Sit beneath the Bodhi tree, where tradition places the Buddha’s enlightenment. Visit a Buddhist temple, an ancient pagoda among the lotuses in the rain. Watch the mist rise around a Taoist sanctuary at dawn. Stand on a Scottish cliff above the ocean, or wait for first light at the center of Stonehenge. Breathe the pure air of a blue ice cave, or rest under the northern lights inside a circle of crystals.

Each session lasts 13 to 17 minutes and is marked as intermediate. They suit you if you love nature, travel and quiet places, and want the setting itself to steady your attention. The voice lingers on light, sound and texture, so each place becomes a calm space you can return to whenever you like.
faq: Do I need to know these places to enjoy the sessions?

Not at all. The voice describes each place in detail: its light, its sounds and its textures. You can picture it clearly, even if you have never been there. You may enjoy discovering these places for the first time through the sessions.
How long are the sessions?

They last between 13 and 17 minutes, long enough to settle into the scene without needing a large block of time. That makes them easy to fit into a lunch break, a quiet evening or the start of a weekend morning.
Are these meditations religious?

They take place in settings linked to different traditions, such as Buddhist sacred spaces or a Taoist sanctuary. They do not ask you to adopt any belief. The focus is on attention, calm and the experience of the place.
What is a Bodhi tree meditation?

It is a meditation beneath the tree where, in Buddhist tradition, the Buddha reached enlightenment. In Beneath the Bodhi Tree, you feel its roots below you and let your attention open like its leaves. It lasts 17 minutes.
Is Stonehenge a Celtic sacred site?
Not quite. Stonehenge is far older than Celtic culture: building began about 5,000 years ago. In At the Center of Stonehenge, you watch dawn reveal the stones one by one.
What are examples of sacred places?

A sacred place is a site that a community sets apart for prayer, ritual or remembrance. Some are built, like a Buddhist pagoda or a Taoist mountain sanctuary. Others are natural, like a tree, a cliff or a cave. The seven sessions here draw on both kinds, from the Bodhi tree in India to the stone circle of Stonehenge in England.
Is there a northern lights meditation?

Yes. The Northern Lights and the Circle of Crystals lasts 15 minutes. You rest under the aurora borealis while a circle of crystals splits its light into hundreds of reflections on the ground. It is a quiet session for the evening, and a good one to replay when you want a sense of wonder.

guide.h2: Meditate in the world’s sacred places
p: Each session takes you, in your imagination, to a place where people have meditated for centuries: beneath the Bodhi tree, inside Stonehenge, in a Taoist mountain sanctuary.

You settle in, listen and breathe with the place. It is a little like a non-religious pilgrimage made from your chair. For real pilgrim routes, the blog follows the Camino de Santiago and the Shikoku pilgrimage in Japan.

guide.h2: Sacred space meditation: a place you can return to
p: This kind of meditation gives you a sacred space of your own: an inner place that feels protected and meaningful, somewhere to rest for a few minutes. Any of these seven settings can become that place. Choose the one that moved you most and listen to it several times, until its light, its sounds and its air come back easily.

After that, a few slow breaths and one remembered detail are often enough to return there, with no audio. If you would rather build a refuge that exists nowhere on Earth, The Floating Island world is a safe place visualization.

guide.h2: A good first journey
p: At the Center of Stonehenge and The Scottish Cliff Above the Ocean last 13 minutes each, an easy way in. For a full temple meditation, The Ancient Temple world takes you up to a mountain temple lit by candles. For a monastery meditation, the Monastery at Sunrise world opens high in the Himalayas, just before dawn.

guides.seo: Spirit Guide Meditation: Meet Your Guide in {n} Free Journeys
guides.desc: Spirit guide meditation, no dogma required: {n} free guided journeys of {min} to {max} minutes to meet your spirit guide or a council of guides. No ads.
guides.h1: Spirit guide meditation: guided journeys to meet your guides
intro: Spirit Guides offers five spirit guide meditations, each one a calm inner journey to meet your spirit guide. Walk down ten steps to the Temple of Light, receive the warmth of a guide of light and keep it after the guide steps away, or consult a council of five guides about a problem before taking the sixth seat yourself. One session gives you a name and a sign to find this inner state again, and another invites you to thank the people who have mattered in your life.

Sessions last 16 to 26 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit anyone curious about imaginative inner journeys, whatever their beliefs. Find a quiet moment, ideally with headphones, and let each image or feeling come in its own time, without trying to force a particular experience.
faq: Do I need to believe in spirit guides?

No. You can approach these sessions as imaginative journeys that help you listen to yourself differently. Whatever you believe, the practice stays the same: relax, follow the voice and notice what comes.
What is the best meditation to connect with spirit guides?
The Ten Steps to the Temple of Light is a good first step, as it guides you into a calm state. The Name and the Sign then gives you a simple way to return to that state later.
What happens if I do not see anything?

That is common and perfectly fine. Some people perceive images, others feelings, words or simply a sense of presence. The sessions do not ask you to force anything, and the experience often becomes richer as you return to them over time.
What happens in a spirit guide meditation?
You relax, visualize a peaceful place and let a guide appear in whatever form comes. Many people receive a feeling, a word or an image rather than a clear figure.
Is this a guided meditation to connect with spirit guides and angels?
It can be. In The Guide of Light, a guide dressed in white or a pale color comes to meet you. If you picture an angel, that is welcome: the session then becomes an angel spirit guide meditation.
What is a spirit guide?

In many spiritual traditions, a spirit guide is a benevolent presence that accompanies and advises a person: an ancestor, an animal, an angel or a figure of light. Some people see it instead as a way of picturing their own intuition. These sessions work with either view. The complete guide to spirit guides, linked on this page, goes through the different kinds.
Can you meet your spirit guides in your sleep?

Some people report meeting a guide in a dream. These sessions do not try to make that happen: they are done awake, and each one ends with a return. If you drift off in the evening, nothing is lost. To catch what comes at night, keep a dream journal within reach and write in it as soon as you wake up.
Is there a 5-minute spirit guide meditation for beginners?

Not one that short: settling into a calm state takes longer, and the shortest session, The Name and the Sign, lasts 16 minutes. For a first try, start with The Ten Steps to the Temple of Light, which walks you down slowly. Later, the name or the sign you received can bring that state back in a few quiet breaths.

guide.h2: How to meet your spirit guide
p: Each spirit guide visualization starts with deep relaxation and a peaceful inner place. Then a presence comes to meet you: a light, a figure, an animal or simply a feeling.
There is no right form. If an animal comes, the journey becomes an animal spirit guide meditation. Welcome what appears and let it unfold.
If you are looking for a spirit animal in particular, the blog shows how to find yours in five steps.

guide.h2: Which spirit guide meditation should you start with?
p: Not sure how to connect with your spirit guides? The Name and the Sign is the shortest, 16 minutes: you ask for a name or a sign to find your guide again. For a 20-minute spirit guide meditation, try The Ten Steps to the Temple of Light (21 min). The Guide of Light, a classic meet-your-spirit-guide meditation, and The Council of Guides take the meeting further.

guide.h2: How to communicate with your spirit guides: one question at a time
p: A guide is easier to hear when you bring something precise. In The Council of Guides, you put one real question into a single sentence and set it at the center of a round table. Five guides look at it in turn: compassion, action, creativity, the body, relationships. Each one asks you something from that angle, and you listen to your own answer. Then you take the sixth seat yourself.

Whether you see guides as presences or as sides of your own mind, the method is the same: ask one clear question, listen without arguing, and write down what you heard. In the app, the Spiritual Experiences notebook is made for this, next to the Dream Journal.

higherKnowledge.seo: Free Akashic Records Meditation and Grief Meditations
higherKnowledge.desc: Akashic Records meditation and gentle grief meditation: {n} guided journeys of {min} to {max} minutes, the archive keeper and a garden of reunion. Free, no ads.
higherKnowledge.h1: A guided journey to the Akashic Records, and gentle reunions beyond loss
intro: Higher Knowledge & Beyond holds three longer journeys, beginning with an Akashic Records meditation. In The Keeper of the Archives, you learn to tell what the mind invents from what seems to arise on its own. The Garden of Reunion is both a grief meditation and a meditation to connect with ancestors: you say the words left unsaid, then feel what passes from one generation to the next. My Departed Animal is a gentle pet loss meditation, built on everyday memories of an animal who has passed.

Each session lasts 24 to 25 minutes and is marked as intermediate. They are best enjoyed when you have time and a quiet space, and they suit anyone drawn to memory, family ties and inner exploration. Emotions may come up along the way, so give yourself a calm moment afterwards before returning to your day.
faq: What are the Akashic records?

The Akashic records are described as a kind of memory said to hold every experience. In The Keeper of the Archives, the focus stays practical: noticing what your mind builds and what seems to appear by itself, without asking you to adopt any belief.
Is My Departed Animal suitable after a recent loss?
The session works gently with everyday memories of your animal. Emotions may come up, and that is natural. Listen when you feel ready, and feel free to pause whenever you need to.
How much time should I set aside?
Plan for around half an hour. The sessions last 24 to 25 minutes, and it is worth taking a quiet moment afterwards, perhaps to write a few notes, before returning to the rest of your day.
Is this an Akashic Records reading, free of charge?

Not in the usual sense: nobody reads your records for you. The Keeper of the Archives lets you explore them yourself, as a guided inner journey. It is free, like the whole app, with no account and no ads.
Is an Akashic Records meditation dangerous?

It is a guided visualization: you stay awake and you can open your eyes at any time. What can surprise you is emotion, above all in the two reunion sessions, where a memory may bring tears. If you are going through a fragile period, wait until you feel ready, and treat what you see as images, not as instructions for your life.

guide.h2: How does a guided meditation for Akashic Records work?
p: In some spiritual traditions, the Akashic Records, or Akashic Chronicles, hold the memory of every soul. Here you explore them as an inner library, welcomed by an Akashic record keeper.
Treat this meditation to access Akashic Records as a symbolic journey, without expectations.
Wondering how to access the Akashic Records? This is a gentle way in: an oak door, a keeper and one question, asked once.
For another walk among the shelves, The Celestial Library world is an Akashic library lit by floating candles.

guide.h2: Akashic Records meaning: where the idea comes from
p: Akasha is a Sanskrit word for sky, space or ether. In the late 1800s, Theosophists taught that this ether keeps a trace of every thought and event, and called it the Akashic Records. In the twentieth century, the American psychic Edgar Cayce made the idea widely known.
Are the Akashic Records real? That is a matter of belief: nobody has shown that such a record exists outside the mind, and this meditation does not ask you to decide. It simply borrows the image.

guide.h2: Gentle reunions: a grief meditation at your own pace
p: The Garden of Reunion and My Departed Animal offer a tender moment with someone you loved, in a calm and gentle setting.

shamanic.seo: Shamanic Journey Meditation: {n} Free Guided Journeys
shamanic.desc: A shamanic journey for the imagination: {n} guided shamanic meditations of {min} to {max} minutes, from the vision quest to the fire of the ancients. Free, no ads.
shamanic.h1: Guided shamanic journey meditation for the imagination
intro: Shamanic Trance offers four inner journeys, each one a guided shamanic journey meditation inspired by tradition. The Vision Quest is about walking, waiting and letting what needs to be seen arrive. In The Fire of the Ancients, you watch the figures gathering by the fire without forcing a message. The Circle of Protection draws on the element that calls you, and the last journey brings you back with a power object to recognize and hold.

Sessions last 23 to 30 minutes and are marked as intermediate. Shamanic meditation of this kind suits you if you already have some experience with relaxation and want to explore deeper imaginative journeys. Lie down or sit comfortably, ideally with headphones, and let the voice lead you from the start of the journey all the way back.
faq: What is a shamanic journey?

In many traditions, a shamanic journey is an inner voyage, often supported by a steady drumbeat, to other worlds and their symbols. Here it is offered as a guided meditation you follow with your imagination, lying down or seated.
Do I need a drum?

No. The session guides you entirely by voice, so there is no instrument to play or prepare. All you need is a quiet place where you will not be disturbed, your phone and, ideally, a pair of headphones to stay immersed.
Is it suitable if I have never meditated?
These sessions are marked as intermediate and last up to 30 minutes. If you are new, start with Learning Basics to get used to relaxing and following the voice, then come back to these journeys.
Is this a shamanic drumming meditation?
Not quite: these four journeys are guided by voice alone, with no drum to hear. For a drum meditation, try Journey to the Lower World in Trances & Techniques: you imagine a steady drum.
What is shamanic meditation?

It is a guided meditation built like a shamanic journey: you leave, explore an inner landscape and come back. In place of a drum and a ceremony, a voice sets the scene and your imagination does the traveling. It asks for no belief: what you meet can simply be taken as an image that says something about you.
What is a vision quest meditation?

A vision quest is a rite found among several Native American peoples: time spent alone in nature, waiting for a vision. The Vision Quest session borrows only its outline, in imagination: for thirty minutes, you walk, wait and let what needs to be seen arrive. It is not the traditional rite, which belongs to the peoples who practice it.

guide.h2: What a guided shamanic journey feels like
p: Traditionally, shamanic drumming carries the inner journey with a steady beat. You travel through a landscape, meet presences and come back with something: an image, an object, an answer.
Here the voice guides you on the way out and on the way back. Many traditions map the journey onto three worlds (lower, middle and upper), joined by a world tree.

guide.h2: How to do a shamanic journey at home
p: Shamanic journeying takes little preparation. Choose a time when no one will disturb you for half an hour, lie down or sit, and put on headphones. You can hold a simple question in mind, or none at all.

Then let the voice set the scene and follow it without steering: the images that come on their own are the ones worth watching. When the session brings you back, move your hands and feet, then write down what you saw while it is still fresh.

guide.h2: Where to begin
p: The Circle of Protection, 23 minutes, sets a safe frame. Then The Fire of the Ancients and The Vision Quest go deeper. Returning with a Power Object closes the cycle.

guide.h2: What is my power animal, and where can I meet it?
p: These four journeys do not set out to find an animal, though one may cross your path. In shamanic traditions, a power animal is a helper in animal form, met during a journey, not chosen from a list. The blog explains how to find your spirit animal in five steps.
In the app, Journey to the Lower World, in Trances & Techniques, lets an animal come to you, and The Wolf Spirit Forest world is a wolf spirit animal meditation under the northern lights.

buddhist.seo: Buddhist Meditation: {n} Free Guided Bodhisattva Journeys
buddhist.desc: Guided Buddhist meditation with the bodhisattvas of Mahayana Buddhism: {n} sessions of {min} to {max} minutes for compassion and clarity. Free, no ads.
buddhist.h1: Guided Buddhist meditation in the footsteps of the bodhisattvas
intro: Buddhist Meditations follows the great figures of the Mahayana tradition, most of them bodhisattvas, one guided Buddhist meditation at a time. Walk with Sudhana from teacher to teacher, meet the eleven faces of Avalokiteśvara, cut through looping thoughts with Mañjuśrī’s sword, or go down with his lion into the valley of old fears. Carry Kṣitigarbha’s light into the dark realms, revisit Samantabhadra’s ten vows, climb up to Maitreya’s garden and find a way out of eight dangers with Tārā.

Sessions last 20 to 30 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit practitioners curious about Buddhism and anyone who enjoys meditations rich in imagery and meaning. No belief is required: each figure serves as a guide to explore a quality such as wisdom, compassion or clarity in your own life.
faq: Do I need to be Buddhist?

No. These sessions draw on Buddhist figures and stories, but they focus on qualities everyone can explore, such as wisdom, compassion and clarity. No belief or prior knowledge of Buddhism is required to follow them.
What is a bodhisattva?

In Mahayana Buddhism, a bodhisattva is someone devoted to the awakening of all beings. It follows the path once walked by Gautama Buddha. Zen Buddhism grew from the same tradition. Each bodhisattva embodies a quality, and the sessions use them as guides for reflection.
Which session should I start with?
Mañjuśrī’s Sword, at 20 minutes, is a good entry point: it works with the sentences that keep looping in your head. Sudhana’s Journey, the longest at 30 minutes, gives a broader view of the path.
Is this the same as loving kindness meditation?
It shares the same heart: kindness toward yourself and others. Here it is practiced as a guided journey with a bodhisattva, rather than by repeating phrases.
Do these journeys come from Tibetan Buddhist meditation?
Partly. Tārā and the eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara hold a central place in Tibetan meditation. The other figures, such as Mañjuśrī and Maitreya, are honored across the Mahayana, from Tibet to Japan.
Where does Zen fit in?

Zen is a Mahayana school too. The history of Zen begins with the Chan masters of China. In Japan, Soto Zen Buddhism teaches “just sitting”, in silence. For a guided zen meditation, try The Zen Garden world.
Is this Buddhist meditation for beginners?

Yes, if you have already meditated a little. The sessions are marked as intermediate and last 20 to 30 minutes, but they need no knowledge of Buddhism: each one introduces its figure in a few words, then guides you step by step. If you have never meditated, start with Learning Basics, then come back for Mañjuśrī’s Sword.
Is there a 20-minute guided Buddhist meditation?

Four of the eight journeys last exactly 20 minutes: Mañjuśrī’s Sword, Mañjuśrī’s Lion, Samantabhadra and the White Elephant, and Maitreya’s Garden. Each one is complete in itself, from the first breath to the moment you open your eyes. The others run from 21 to 30 minutes.
Is there a free Buddhist meditation app with no ads?

Yes. MeditaDream is free, with no ads, no subscription and no account. These eight guided journeys are part of it, alongside qigong sessions and The Zen Garden world. Download a journey once and it plays without a signal, even in airplane mode.

guide.h2: Bodhisattva meditation: compassion, clarity and protection
p: In Buddhist tradition, each bodhisattva embodies a quality. Avalokiteśvara, also known as Guanyin Bodhisattva, stands for compassion. Mañjuśrī stands for clarity, and the bodhisattva Tārā, much loved in Tibetan Buddhism, for protection. These guided journeys let you meet them and grow that quality in yourself.

You do not need to be Buddhist. The figures are a support for attention and kindness. If you would rather repeat the traditional phrases, the blog explains metta loving kindness meditation step by step.

guide.h2: Buddhist meditation techniques: which journey to choose
p: Wondering how to meditate? Buddhism offers many paths, and here each journey follows a great Mahayana figure. For a Buddhist compassion meditation, choose The Eleven Faces of Avalokiteśvara. For clarity, Mañjuśrī’s Sword. For a gentle look at who you are becoming, Maitreya’s Garden. Outside this category, The Ancient Temple world offers a Buddhist temple meditation among candles and stone Buddhas.

guide.h2: Buddhism and meditation: where these journeys come from
p: Buddhism and meditation have gone together from the start: tradition says the Buddha awakened while sitting in meditation under the Bodhi tree. Centuries later, the Mahayana schools added a wealth of stories and images, and these eight journeys borrow from them. Sudhana’s pilgrimage from teacher to teacher comes from an old Mahayana text, the Gandavyuha Sutra, which closes with Samantabhadra’s ten great vows. Kṣitigarbha, shown as a monk, vowed to help beings in the realms of suffering, and Maitreya is the Buddha to come.
Each session is a free interpretation: a Mahayana Buddhist meditation in images, made for reflection rather than religious instruction.

qigong.seo: Qigong Meditation for Beginners: {n} Free Guided Sessions
qigong.desc: Qigong meditation for beginners, guided and free: {n} sessions of {min} to {max} minutes, from warm hands to the still tree. No class fees, works offline.
qigong.h1: Qigong meditation: feel the Qi, no experience needed
intro: Sensations & Qigong is qigong for beginners in its quietest form: it uses qigong meditation to turn your attention to the body in inner motion. Start by warming the hands around an imaginary ball, then follow the small circulation, a pearl descending from the belly and rising along the back. The Still Tree is a standing grounding meditation, arms around an imaginary ball, rooted without forcing. The last session, The Dance of Qi, brings qigong into motion until the body seems to move on its own.

Sessions last 20 to 25 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit you if you like gentle movement, standing practice and paying close attention to physical sensations. No prior knowledge is needed, so they also work as qigong meditation for beginners. The voice describes each posture, and you only need a little space around you to move freely.
faq: Do I need to know qigong?

No prior knowledge is needed. The voice explains each posture and each step. If you have practiced qigong before, you will recognize classic exercises such as the still tree and the small circulation.
Should I sit or stand?
It depends on the session. Warming the Hands and The Small Circulation can be done seated, while The Still Tree and The Dance of Qi invite you to stand. Choose a space where you can move a little.
What is the small circulation, or microcosmic orbit meditation?

It is a classic qigong practice that follows a path through the body, down the front and up the back, in a loop. In the session, you follow it with your attention, like a pearl moving slowly along the way.
Can I do qigong meditation sitting down?
Yes. Warming the Hands and The Small Circulation work well seated. The Still Tree is traditionally done standing, but you can adapt it.
Is MeditaDream a qigong app?

It is a meditation app that includes these four qigong sessions, free and without ads. You need no account, and each session plays offline once downloaded. For corrections on posture, a live teacher remains the best complement.
What is Qi meditation?

Qi meditation is a common name for the quiet, attentive side of qigong. Instead of learning a long sequence of movements, you rest your attention on what you feel, such as warmth in the palms, tingling or a sense of flow, and let the breath slow down. What is Qi? Also written chi, it is the word Chinese traditions use for this felt energy. No belief is required: you can take it simply as sensation.
What are the main qigong meditation techniques?

Four simple ones run through these sessions. Holding an imaginary ball between the palms wakes up sensation in the hands. The small circulation, or microcosmic orbit, takes your attention around a loop through the body. Zhan zhuang is the practice of standing still like a tree. Moving qigong lets slow gestures carry your attention. Each technique has its own session, so you can learn them one at a time.
Is qigong meditation good before sleep?

The two seated sessions, Warming the Hands and The Small Circulation, are slow and quiet, so they fit well into an evening. They are not designed to put you to sleep, though. For that, the Body, Calm & Sleep category has sessions made for bedtime, such as Drifting into Sleep, which ends with no wake-up.

guide.h2: What is qigong meditation?
p: Qigong meditation is the quiet side of qigong. Chinese teachers describe it through three regulations: the body, the breath and the mind. You adjust them one after the other, until they settle together. You will also see it written qi gong, chi gong or chi kung meditation: the practice is the same, only the spelling changes.

It comes in two forms. Still qigong is practiced seated or standing without moving, like zhan zhuang, the standing posture that The Still Tree follows. Moving qigong lets slow gestures carry your attention, as in The Dance of Qi.
Attention often rests on the lower dantian, a point a few fingers below the navel. This simple anchor is what makes qigong a meditation, not just a gentle exercise.

guide.h2: Qigong for beginners: what you will feel
p: Many people turn to qigong for vitality and calm. This Chinese practice links breath, attention and slow movement. These sessions focus on what you feel inside: warmth, tingling, a sense of energy moving.
Most people feel warmth in their hands within the first session. The Still Tree doubles as a grounding exercise: you stand rooted, without forcing.

guide.h2: Guided qigong meditation: a simple order
p: Start with Warming the Hands, then The Still Tree, a standing tree meditation. The Small Circulation follows the energy along the body, and The Dance of Qi brings it all into motion. Keep your qigong breathing slow and natural throughout.

Taken in this order, the four sessions work like a short series of qigong meditation lessons, one technique at a time. For movements to go with them, the blog has a 10-minute routine of qigong exercises for beginners.

visualisation.seo: Free Guided Visualization Meditation: Train Your Inner Eye
visualisation.desc: Can’t “see” anything when you visualize? {n} guided visualization and guided imagery meditations of {min} to {max} minutes train one sense at a time. Free, no ads.
visualisation.h1: Guided visualization meditation to train your inner eye
intro: Visualization meditation, also called guided imagery meditation, trains your imagination one sense at a time. Follow a butterfly’s flight with your inner eye, feel the weight and coldness of a key in your open hand, or track a singing bowl approaching from afar with your inner ear. Then bring the senses together at the summit of an extinct volcano or in a spaceship cockpit, and finally rebuild a room you know by heart as the evening light falls into it.

Sessions last 16 to 29 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit anyone who finds it hard to picture things. They also prepare deeper journeys, from a safe place visualization to the immersive worlds. Working on one sense at a time makes progress easier, and the skills you build here carry over to the rest of the app.
faq: What if I cannot see images in my mind?
That is very common. These sessions work on each sense separately, so you can start with touch or hearing if images feel difficult. Visualization is a skill that grows with practice.
What is the difference between visualization and meditation?

Visualization is one way of meditating. Instead of only observing what is there, you build sights, sounds or sensations in your imagination. It trains attention and makes the longer guided journeys in the app richer and easier to follow.
In what order should I do these visualization exercises?
Start with the single-sense sessions, the butterfly, the key and the singing bowl, then move on to the sessions that combine the three senses. The Room You Know is a good one to finish with.
How can I learn how to visualize during meditation?
Start with sound and touch, which are often easier than pictures. Then add sight, one short session at a time. Visual images tend to follow with regular practice.
Is there a free guided imagery app?

Yes. MeditaDream gives you every guided visualization free, with no subscription, no ads and no account. Its visualization sessions and 17 immersive worlds work as guided imagery recordings you can play offline.
Is this visualization meditation for beginners?

Yes: you can be new to visualization, as long as you have meditated a little. The sessions are marked as intermediate and last 16 to 29 minutes, and the first three each train a single skill: following a movement, feeling a weight, placing a sound. Start with Hearing — the Distant Singing Bowl, the shortest at 16 minutes.
Can I use guided imagery meditation for sleep?

These six sessions ask for active attention, so they suit the daytime or early evening, and each one ends with your eyes open. For guided imagery at bedtime, choose Sleep Journey in Body, Calm & Sleep: a garden, a still pool and a house turning off its lights, with no wake-up at the end.

guide.h2: Is visualization meditation the same as guided imagery meditation?
p: The two are very close: both build a scene in your mind. Mental visualization is not only about seeing clear pictures. It also means hearing, touching and feeling in your imagination. Think of each session as guided imagery relaxation with one goal: training a sense.
With practice, images become brighter and more stable. Here is how to improve visualization: one sense first, a little every day.

guide.h2: How to visualize for beginners: from one sense to all three
p: Start with Hearing — the Distant Singing Bowl, then Touch — the Key in Your Hand. When those feel easy, the Three Senses sessions take you to a volcano summit or across the galaxy.

If pictures refuse to come, do not push. Begin with what you can call up easily: the weight of a key in your palm, the fading note of a bowl. Hold one detail for a few breaths, then add a second, such as temperature or distance. When the session ends, compare what you imagined with a real sensation: that back-and-forth helps the image grow sharper. Sight often comes last, and a blurry outline counts.

miniAdventures.seo: Story Meditation: Guided Journeys and Time-Travel Adventures
miniAdventures.desc: Story meditation as time travel: Versailles in 1700, the road to Kyoto, an unknown planet. {n} guided journeys of {min} to {max} minutes. Free, no ads.
miniAdventures.h1: Guided story meditation: one place, one time, one story
intro: Mini Adventures offers a complete journey in a single session: a story meditation with a place, a time and a tale to step into. Spend a whole day at the court of Versailles in 1700, walk the road to Kyoto in 1600 with your senses wide awake, or explore an unknown planet and notice how each question changes the way you look. The Train of Memories takes you station after station through the habits, tastes and decisions that shape a life.

Sessions last 17 to 34 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit you if you enjoy stories, history and travel, and want a longer, immersive escape. Choose a quiet evening or a slow weekend morning, settle in comfortably, and let each scene unfold at its own calm and unhurried pace.
faq: Are these meditations or audio stories?
Both, in a way. They are guided meditations that tell a story: you relax first, then live the journey with all your senses, at a calm pace and with pauses to take in each scene.
Do I need to know about history?

No. The voice gives you everything you need to picture Versailles in 1700 or the road to Kyoto in 1600. You can simply relax and let yourself be carried along, discovering the details as the story unfolds.
How much time should I set aside?
They last from 17 minutes for the unknown planet to 34 minutes for the road to Kyoto. Choose a moment when you will not be disturbed, such as a quiet evening or a weekend.
Is a guided journey still meditation?
Yes. You stay relaxed and attentive to what you imagine. This kind of journeying meditation is a gentle way to escape for a while.
Can I use a story meditation for sleep?

You can listen at night, but these four keep you gently present and end by bringing you back to the room, eyes open. They are not sleep stories for adults that fade out as you drift off. If sleep is the goal, choose Sleep Journey in Body, Calm & Sleep: 27 minutes with no wake-up at the end.
Are these guided meditation stories for adults?

Yes. They are written for adults: 17 to 34 minutes each, slow and rich in detail, with pauses to take in every scene. A curious teenager can enjoy the road to Kyoto or the unknown planet, but young children will probably find them long.

guide.h2: A guided journey you can get lost in
p: Each session is a meditation adventure: Versailles in 1700, the road to Kyoto in 1600, an unknown planet. Unlike a pure fantasy meditation, two of them are rooted in real history.
There is nothing to learn. You simply let the story carry you, relaxed and present.
Each journey doubles as a guided visualization meditation: the voice names what you see, hear and touch.

guide.h2: Time travel meditation: Versailles in 1700, Kyoto in 1600
p: “Versailles — a Day in 1700” begins in a carriage along the Seine, then leads you through the Hall of Mirrors as Louis XIV passes and out to a banquet in the gardens. “Japan — on the Road to Kyoto in 1600” moves at walking pace: a mountain road in the morning mist, a bamboo forest, an old temple with its Zen garden, and a small package to deliver at a teahouse.
Both are written for the senses, and you are never tested on dates.

guide.h2: How long they last
p: The Unknown Planet, a space meditation of 17 minutes, is the shortest. Each time travel meditation is richer and lasts up to 34 minutes.

thirdEye.seo: Third Eye Chakra Meditation: How to Open Your Third Eye
thirdEye.desc: Third eye chakra meditation without forcing it: {n} advanced guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes on Ajna, to open your third eye gently. Free, no ads.
thirdEye.h1: Guided third eye meditation on the Ajna chakra
intro: Third Eye is a set of third eye chakra meditations, all focused on the point between the brows: an unhurried way to open your third eye. You start by feeling both physical eyes, then learn to shift from looking outward to looking inward. Other sessions let an image be born at the center of the forehead and fade away, invite you to wait before the dark space until an image appears on its own, take you through the door of Ajna, or let a mandala keep building itself once you let go of control.

Sessions last 22 to 26 minutes and are marked as advanced. They are best approached after some practice with relaxation and visualization meditation. Start with The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes, which teaches the shift of attention that the other sessions build on, and take your time with each one.
faq: What is the third eye?
In several traditions, the third eye, or Ajna, refers to the point between the eyebrows, associated with inner perception. In these sessions, it serves as a focus point for attention and imagination.
Are these sessions for beginners?

They are marked as advanced. If you are new to meditation, try the Learning Basics and Visualization categories first, then come back here once you are used to holding your attention for twenty minutes or more.
Where should I start?

The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes is the natural first step. It teaches the shift from looking outward to looking inward that the other sessions build on, so it is worth repeating it a few times before moving on.
How do you open the third eye with meditation?
Sit comfortably, rest your attention between the eyebrows and let images appear on their own. The Inner Eye Awakens is a gentle meditation to open third eye vision, step by step, without promises.
Is this a pineal gland activation meditation?

Not in a physical sense. Some traditions link the third eye to the pineal gland, but these sessions make no claim about the body. Here, third eye activation simply means training attention and inner images between the brows.
Is seeing colors during meditation normal?
Yes, it is common when you rest your attention between the brows with your eyes closed. Welcome the colors without chasing them, as the sessions suggest. If none appear, that is fine too.
Where is the third eye chakra?

Between the eyebrows, slightly above the bridge of the nose. In the yoga map of seven chakras, it is the sixth, called Ajna, above the throat and below the crown. Traditions link it to intuition and inner sight. In these sessions, it is simply the spot where you rest your attention. For a guided chakra meditation through all seven centers, try Chakra Reset, in Body, Calm & Sleep.

guide.h2: How to open your third eye, gently
p: The third eye, or Ajna chakra, is the point between the eyebrows in yoga tradition. You rest your attention there and let inner images come, without chasing them.

Third eye awakening takes time, so these sessions are advanced. Some ease with visualization helps. Want to know how to activate third eye vision? There is no switch, just attention you train session after session.

In practice, it comes down to four steps. Let the body and the breath settle, and relax the forehead. Feel both physical eyes, one after the other, without moving them. Rest your attention between the brows, lightly. Then watch the dark space behind your eyelids and let whatever appears come and go. If the forehead tightens, you are forcing: ease off and return to the breath.
For the story behind the symbol, from the Ajna chakra to the pineal gland, the blog looks at the third eye meaning in detail.

guide.h2: Third eye meditation techniques: a possible progression
p: Begin with The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes, a gentle third eye chakra meditation. Next comes The Inner Eye Awakens. Then try The Image that Appears on its Own and The Mandala that Builds Itself, where you simply watch. The Door of Ajna, a pure Ajna chakra meditation, takes you through to the place beyond.

These sessions keep your attention in your head. Afterward, come back to the body: stand up, feel your feet, look around the room. The blog’s guide to the root chakra lists five grounding exercises for exactly this.

cosmic.seo: Free Spiritual Awakening Meditation: Non-Dual Awareness
cosmic.desc: A taste of spiritual awakening: {n} advanced guided non-dual meditations of {min} to {max} minutes, awareness without edges and a body of light. Free, no ads.
cosmic.h1: Guided non-dual meditation for spiritual awakening
intro: Cosmic & Void holds two advanced sessions for a taste of spiritual awakening, beyond the familiar: a non-dual meditation and a light body meditation. In Non-dual Awareness, you look for where inside ends and outside begins, then gently turn toward the one who perceives. In Light Body Expansion, you start from the simple warmth of your body and let it grow into a light that reaches beyond the skin and into the space around you.

The sessions last 28 and 31 minutes and are marked as advanced. They suit experienced meditators drawn to vastness, open awareness or higher consciousness. Set aside a quiet half hour, sit or lie down comfortably, and let the questions do their work without trying to reach a particular state.
faq: What is non-duality?

Non-duality refers to the experience of not separating the observer from what is observed. The session approaches it through simple questions, such as where inside ends and outside begins, rather than through theory. The same question runs through Advaita meditation and many Buddhist schools.
Do I need experience?

Ideally, yes. These two sessions are marked as advanced and last around half an hour each. Some familiarity with longer meditations helps, for example the Trance category or a cosmic meditation like The Cosmic Temple world.
Which session should I try first?

Light Body Expansion starts from a physical sensation, warmth, which makes it a little more concrete. Non-dual Awareness then takes you further, toward the question of who is actually perceiving, so it makes sense to try them in that order.
What is non-dual meditation?
A practice where you stop separating the one who observes from what is observed, and simply rest in presence.
Is spiritual awakening the same as spiritual enlightenment?

The two are close. Full enlightenment, Buddhism says, is a complete and lasting awakening, and Zen calls a sudden glimpse of it satori. These sessions make no such promise: they offer a calm taste of open, non-dual awareness.
Is this a void meditation?
In a way. Cosmic & Void points toward the open space in which thoughts and sensations appear. You rest in that space rather than trying to empty the mind.
What is the difference between mindfulness and non-dual mindfulness?

In mindfulness, you observe an object, such as the breath or a sound. In non-dual meditation, sometimes called non-dual mindfulness, you turn toward what is observing and notice that awareness and what it knows are not two separate things. Mindfulness is the usual way in: steady attention comes first.
Is MeditaDream a non-dual meditation app?

It is a meditation app with a small non-dual corner: these two advanced sessions, free and without ads. You need no account, and each session plays offline once downloaded. If non-dual practice becomes your main path, a teacher remains a good complement.

guide.h2: What is the meaning of spiritual awakening?
p: In many contemplative traditions, a spiritual awakening is a shift in how you experience yourself: the sense of being a separate observer, set apart from the world, loosens for a moment or for good. That absence of separation is what the word non-duality points to, and what many people mean by awakening.
Teachers often speak of stages, or levels of consciousness, yet most agree that it cannot be forced. Meditation only sets up the conditions: a mind quiet and curious enough to look.

guide.h2: Spiritual awakening: what non-dual awareness feels like
p: In non-dual awareness, the line between you and everything else softens. What remains is simple, open presence. That is why some call this practice a oneness meditation.
These sessions are long and advanced, close to half an hour. Some practice helps.

guide.h2: Meditation on emptiness and light: two journeys
p: Non-dual Awareness, a classic non-dual awareness meditation, invites you to rest in open space. Light Body Expansion becomes a universe meditation, as your body seems to widen all the way to the stars. If you are looking for a cosmic consciousness meditation, start there.
For a shorter cosmic meditation to begin with, The Cosmic Temple world lasts 13 minutes.

trance.seo: Waking Dream and Trance Meditation: {n} Free Guided Sessions
trance.desc: Waking dream and trance meditation, body asleep, mind awake: {n} guided sessions of {min} to {max} minutes, from a 33-level spiral to your future self. Free, no ads.
trance.h1: Waking dream meditation: guided trance, body asleep and mind awake
intro: Consciousness & Trance explores the waking dream and other borders of ordinary awareness, one guided trance meditation at a time. In Body Asleep, Mind Awake, you feel asleep but awake, watching the threshold of sleep. You can descend a 33-level spiral, wander an infinite library while staying connected to your body, or explore an attic of forgotten objects. Other sessions offer a directed waking dream, a rest in the space between two thoughts, and a meeting with your future self.

Sessions last 20 to 32 minutes and are marked as intermediate. They suit you if you are curious about deep relaxation and imaginative states. Each session guides you gently back at the end. Listen somewhere comfortable, never while driving, and give yourself a moment to return before getting up.
faq: What is a trance meditation?

A meditative trance is a state of deep relaxation in which attention narrows and imagination becomes more vivid. You remain aware throughout the session, you can open your eyes at any moment, and the voice always brings you gently back at the end.
Is it safe?

These sessions are guided and always bring you back gently. You stay in control the whole time. As with any deep relaxation, do not listen while driving or doing anything that requires your attention.
Which session should I start with?
The 33-level Spiral is a good introduction, since the count guides you step by step. Body Asleep, Mind Awake is ideal if you are interested in the threshold of sleep.
What is a waking dream?

A waking dream is a guided daydream: you stay awake while images unfold as in a dream. In Directed Waking Dream, a guided thread starts the story and spontaneous images change it. The voice guides you in and brings you back.
What is a hypnagogic meditation?
It works with the hypnagogic state, the drowsy edge between waking and sleep. Body Asleep, Mind Awake trains you to stay aware at that threshold. Images often appear there on their own.
Trance vs meditation: what is the difference?

Mindfulness meditation trains you to stay with what is here: the breath, the body, passing thoughts. A trance narrows your attention and lets imagination lead, as in a daydream. These sessions sit between the two: you relax as in meditation, then follow images down a spiral or along a mountain path, and the voice brings you back at the end.
Is a waking dream the same as a lucid dream?

No. In a lucid dream you are asleep and you know that you are dreaming. In a waking dream you never fall asleep: you lie still, relaxed, and let images unfold while staying aware of the room. For dreams themselves, see the lucid dreaming guide and the Lucid Dream Preparation session.

guide.h2: Guided trance meditation: body asleep, mind awake
p: Your body relaxes deeply while your mind stays awake. In that state, images come easily: an infinite library, a spiral, a forgotten attic.
That is the state these sessions help you reach.
It is a mild altered state of consciousness, a close cousin of daydreaming, and at the edge of sleep it has a name: the hypnagogic state, or hypnagogia.
The blog article “Trance Meaning” shows how everyday this state is, from a gripping novel to a long drive.

guide.h2: How to go into a trance: where to begin
p: Directed Waking Dream and The Attic of Forgotten Objects last 20 minutes. Body Asleep, Mind Awake teaches the basic state.

Here is how to go into a trance with these sessions. Lie down in a position you could fall asleep in. Breathe out slowly once or twice, then leave your breathing alone. Let the body grow heavy from the feet up while you keep one thread of awareness: “I am still here.” Then give your mind a simple path, such as the steps of a spiral staircase or a mountain trail, and let the images come. At the end, move your fingers and toes before you open your eyes.

tranceTechniques.seo: How to Do Self Hypnosis: {n} Guided Deep Trance Journeys
tranceTechniques.desc: How to do self hypnosis, the gentle way: {n} advanced guided journeys of {min} to {max} minutes, down into a deep, hypnotic trance and back. Free, no ads.
tranceTechniques.h1: How to do self hypnosis, step by step: gentle deep trance journeys
intro: Trances & Techniques shows you how to do self hypnosis gently, through seven advanced deep trance journeys. Learn to go down into trance in stages with brief returns to the surface, follow an animal to the lower world to the sound of the drum, or rise through wind and light to the upper world. Other sessions travel up your family line, reread your soul contract, open the corridor of a thousand doors onto other eras, and borrow a quality from a craftsperson of long ago.

Sessions last 16 to 30 minutes and are marked as advanced: each one is a deep trance guided meditation, not a quick break. Progressive Descent into Trance is the best place to start, since it teaches you to go down and come back up at your own pace. Once that feels familiar, the other journeys become easier to follow and more comfortable.
faq: Is this a past life regression?

No. Past Lives & Time travels up your family line: you see what you want to keep, set down or pass on. For a past life meditation, The Corridor of a Thousand Doors lets you imagine a scene from another era. Neither claims to reveal real past lives, and neither promises a result.
Why start with Progressive Descent into Trance?
This session teaches you to go down in stages and come back to the surface. That skill makes the longer journeys to the lower and upper worlds easier to follow and more comfortable.
What is a soul contract?

It is an image used to reflect on your path: what you are learning, what you have to offer and what you can let go of. The Contract of My Soul, a soul contract meditation, invites you to reread it calmly, with no fixed answer.
Are these journeys for beginners?
No, they are advanced. Start with Body Asleep, Mind Awake in the trance category, then come back here.
What does a hypnotic trance feel like?
Calm and focused, a little like the moment before sleep. Your body grows heavy while your attention narrows on the voice and the images. You stay aware, and you can open your eyes at any time.
Can I use self hypnosis for sleep?
These journeys bring you back at the end, so they are not made for falling asleep. For bedtime, the Body, Calm & Sleep category has sessions with no wake-up, such as Drifting into Sleep.
Trance and hypnosis: what is the difference?

Trance is the state; hypnosis is one way of reaching it. A trance is absorbed, narrowed attention: you know it from a gripping film or from highway hypnosis, when miles go by unnoticed. Hypnosis leads you there on purpose, with a voice and suggestions. In self hypnosis you start the process yourself, here by pressing play and following the journey.

guide.h2: How to do self hypnosis: where to begin
p: Forgotten Talents is the shortest, 16 minutes. Progressive Descent into Trance teaches you to go down step by step.

Here is how to do self hypnosis the way that session teaches it. First you settle. Lying down, you feel the weight of your body and keep three anchors: a sound, the air on your face and the surface under your back. Then you walk down an old stone staircase, with one less thing to keep track of at each step. Last, you come back up three steps before going down again: each brief return makes the next descent deeper. The way back is a slow climb, at your own pace.

guide.h2: Trance induction techniques: going deeper
p: These techniques are advanced. Each journey starts with a slow induction, built from classic self hypnosis techniques such as a heavy body, a slower breath or a countdown. Then it takes you to the lower world, the upper world or a corridor of a thousand doors.
Practice the simpler trance sessions first.

Journey to the Lower World and Journey to the Upper World borrow their map from the shamanic journey: a drum, an animal to follow, a way down between the roots of a great tree or up along a thread of light.

astralMicroDetach.seo: Out of Body Experience: Astral Projection for Beginners
astralMicroDetach.desc: Out of body experience training: {n} guided exercises of {min} to {max} minutes. Astral projection for beginners, one sensation at a time. Free, no ads.
astralMicroDetach.h1: Out of body experience training, one small gesture at a time
intro: An out of body experience, the feeling of perceiving from outside your body, rarely comes all at once. Micro-Detachment breaks it into five small gestures to practice before attempting a full exit. It is astral projection for beginners, taken apart and slowed down. Feel the body’s weight and a gentle pull toward the ceiling. Shift the outline of your body by a few centimeters. Move your point of view to just behind your head, or slide down an imaginary slope. Finally, rehearse sitting up in your mind until it feels almost real.

Sessions last 16 to 20 minutes and are marked as advanced. Practice them before moving on to the Astral Projection category, where each protocol is a full guided astral projection meditation. Each exercise here works like a short astral body meditation, training a sensation you will meet again in the longer protocols. Short, regular practice usually works better than long sessions spaced far apart, so take them one at a time.
faq: Why practice micro-detachment first?
A full astral exit combines several sensations at once. Training them one at a time (lightness, shifting, sitting up) makes each one more familiar before you put them together in a longer session.
How often should I practice out of body experience meditation?
