There is no set schedule. Short, regular practice tends to work better than long sessions spaced far apart. Each exercise lasts 16 to 20 minutes, so it fits easily into a quiet evening.
Is it normal not to feel anything?
Yes. These sensations are subtle and vary from one person to another. The sessions invite you to notice without forcing, and they remain a pleasant relaxation even if nothing particular happens.
What are the best astral projection exercises for beginners?
Short detachment exercises such as The Point Behind Your Head or The Slide. They teach you to recognize the first sensations before longer techniques.
Can you have an out of body experience while awake?

That is what these exercises prepare: the body rests deeply while the mind stays clear. Each session trains one small sensation of detachment, in imagination and attention. Nothing is promised: you explore at your own pace.
Is an out of body experience in a dream the same as one while awake?

Not quite. Many people report an out of body experience in a dream or at the edge of sleep: they seem to float, then realize they were dreaming. In these exercises you stay awake and build each sensation on purpose, in imagination. If you tend to doze off, raise your head a little or practice earlier in the day.
Are out of body exercises safe?

They are exercises in guided imagination: your body rests, you stay awake and you can open your eyes at any moment. Some sensations may surprise you, such as a pull toward the ceiling, a slide or a sense of height. If one of them unsettles you, stop, move your hands and feet and breathe quietly. If you are going through a fragile period, save these exercises for later.

guide.h2: Out of body experience meaning: what people describe
p: An out of body experience, or OBE, is the impression of perceiving from a point outside your physical body: floating above the bed, seeing the room from the ceiling, looking back at yourself. Some traditions call it out of body travel and speak of an astral body leaving the physical one. Researchers describe it as a striking shift in the way we sense where we are. Both readings exist side by side, and these exercises do not ask you to choose.
Here the experience stays small and deliberate: you remain awake, you imagine one precise movement, and you stop whenever you like.

guide.h2: How to have an out of body experience: small steps first
p: Micro-detachment means small inner movements before any exit: a slight shift, a point behind your head, a pull toward the ceiling.
These short sessions build the sensations you will need for a longer guided out of body experience. Think of each one as a short OBE meditation with a single task.

guide.h2: How to astral travel for beginners: a good order
p: Start with The Point Behind Your Head or The Slide, 16 minutes each. Then The Ceiling Magnet and The Phantom Sit-up. This order keeps astral projection for beginners simple, one sensation at a time.

astralJourneys.seo: Guided Astral Projection Meditation: {n} Free Techniques
astralJourneys.desc: Guided astral projection meditation: {n} techniques of {min} to {max} minutes, floating, rope, imaginary fall, plus a guided astral travel meditation. Free, no ads.
astralJourneys.h1: Guided astral projection meditation and astral travel
intro: Astral Projection brings together eleven exit protocols. Each one is a guided astral projection meditation, also known as a guided astral travel meditation. Some work with lightness, like floating toward the ceiling or rising up by pivoting at the pelvis. Others use classic astral projection techniques such as the rope, the imaginary fall or inner limbs. You will also find sessions to move and see in the astral, visualize your double, approach a sensed presence and note what you perceive of a target before checking it.

Sessions last 16 to 41 minutes and are marked as advanced. If you are just starting, practice the Micro-Detachment exercises first. Choose a time when your body is deeply relaxed and you will not be disturbed, and approach each protocol with curiosity rather than expectations about the result.
faq: What is astral projection?

Astral projection describes the feeling of perceiving from outside your physical body. These sessions approach it as a guided experience in imagination and attention, without making any promise about the result.
Which technique should I try first?

Floating Toward the Ceiling and the Rope Technique are among the best-known approaches and make good starting points. If you are looking for an astral projection guided meditation for beginners, the five Micro-Detachment exercises are a useful preparation before these longer protocols.
When is the best time to practice?
Some people prefer a moment when the body is deeply relaxed, in the evening or after waking. The longest sessions last up to 41 minutes, so choose a time when you will not be disturbed.
How do you astral project for the first time?
Lie down, relax deeply and let a guided session lead you through an exit technique, such as the rope or floating. Start with the shorter exercises if you are new, and practice without pressure.
Is astral travel meditation the same as astral projection?

Most people use the two names for the same experience: perceiving as if from outside the body. A guided astral travel meditation simply adds movement once you feel detached. The Movement Techniques session is built for that part.
Can I use a guided astral projection meditation for sleep?

Not really. These sessions ask your mind to stay awake while your body rests, which is the opposite of drifting off. If you fall asleep along the way, nothing is lost: try again when you are more rested, early in the morning for example. To fall asleep on purpose, choose Drifting into Sleep or Sleep Journey in Body, Calm & Sleep.
Is a guided astral projection meditation dangerous?

These sessions are guided relaxation with imagery: you stay in your room and you can stop at any moment by opening your eyes and moving your fingers and toes. Sensations such as floating, rising or falling can surprise you; if one of them worries you, end the session and breathe quietly. If you are going through a fragile period, leave these practices for later.

guide.h2: How to astral project: the method behind these sessions
p: If you are wondering how to do astral projection, most techniques follow the same path. First, deep relaxation, until the body feels heavy and still. Then the mind stays awake while the body drifts toward sleep. Finally, an exit technique gives your attention somewhere to go.
Like any out of body experience meditation, each session guides these stages lying down, eyes closed, at an unhurried pace.

guide.h2: Which guided astral projection meditation should you choose?
p: In the rope technique, astral projection starts with the feeling of climbing hand over hand. Floating toward the ceiling plays with lightness. The imaginary fall uses the sense of dropping. Target sessions add something to observe, then check afterwards.
Try them one at a time and keep the one that works for you. People respond very differently to each. Every astral meditation here is guided from the first breath, so there is nothing to memorize.

guide.h2: Tips that help
p: Practice when you are rested but relaxed: early in the morning works well for many people. Keep a notebook nearby and write down what you noticed, even small sensations.
If the longer protocols feel like too much, start with the shorter astral projection exercises. Treat it all as an inner experience, without pressure or expectations.

worldMeditations.seo: Forest Bathing, Vipassana, Stoic Review: World Meditations
worldMeditations.desc: Forest bathing, Vipassana, Tonglen, the Inner Smile, a Stoic evening review: {n} practices from the world’s traditions, {min} to {max} minutes. Free, no ads.
worldMeditations.h1: World Meditations: {n} traditions, from Vipassana to forest bathing
intro: This category brings together {n} short meditations of {min} to {max} minutes from the world’s great traditions. Try Vipassana and Shamatha, Tibetan Buddhist Tonglen, Japanese Naikan or Shinrin-Yoku, better known as forest bathing. Korean Seon, the Taoist Inner Smile, Christian contemplative prayer, Hasidic Hitbodedut and the Stoic evening review complete the tour.

Each session lets you taste a practice the way its tradition teaches it, with its own gestures and words, without asking you to believe anything. They are free, ad-free and play offline once downloaded.

guide.h2: Which world meditation should you start with?
p: If you are new, start with Vipassana, the insight meditation Buddhism has taught since the Buddha. Watching sensations change is the root of many other practices. Shamatha comes next, to steady a clear attention. For longer sessions rooted in Buddhism, see the Buddhist meditation category.

To open the heart, try Tonglen or the Inner Smile; to look back on your day in the evening, Naikan and its three questions, or the Stoic evening review. The Inner Smile is a Taoist practice, a close cousin of qigong meditation.

guide.h2: What is forest bathing, or shinrin-yoku?
p: Born in Japan, shinrin-yoku is a slow walk in nature that pays attention to everything the senses pick up. This guided forest bathing session leads you step by step, ideally outdoors. At home, it becomes a forest bathing meditation in your imagination. The meaning of forest bathing is in the name: in Japanese, shinrin means forest and yoku means bathing. The term dates from the early 1980s.

guide.h2: How to do forest bathing, step by step
p: You do not need a forest: a park or a tree-lined path will do. Silence your notifications and walk more slowly than usual, with nowhere to get to. Let one sense lead at a time: first the colors around you, then sounds, then textures and the air on your skin.

Stop whenever something holds your attention, and stay as long as it does. On your own, a forest bathing walk of twenty minutes is plenty to begin with. It is close to a walking meditation, only slower and with no set route.

guide.h2: Do you need to be religious?
p: No. Contemplative prayer of silence and Hitbodedut are open to everyone: they offer a form of attention and inner dialogue, without imposing anything.

faq: What is Vipassana meditation?
A meditation from the Buddhist tradition: you observe bodily sensations and notice that they keep changing. The introductory session lets you try it in a few minutes.
What is a Stoic evening review?
An end-of-day review inherited from ancient Greece and Rome: calmly going back over your day, what went well and what you can do better tomorrow.
How do you do Vipassana meditation?

Sit in a stable position and follow the belly: note “rising” on the in-breath, “falling” on the out-breath. When a thought or a sound pulls you away, give it one quiet label, such as “thinking” or “hearing,” and come back. Then pick one sensation, warmth or pressure, and watch how it changes. The aim is not to reach a special state, only to notice. The introductory session guides you through this in seven minutes.
What is Tonglen meditation?

Tonglen comes from Tibetan Buddhism, and its name means giving and taking. You breathe in while acknowledging a pain, yours or someone else’s, and breathe out while offering relief. It is a symbolic image, and the six-minute session keeps it gentle: one moderate difficulty at a time, to the rhythm of the breath.

Every world has its own atmosphere, its own soundscape and its own intention, from grounding and safety to wonder and clarity. antiqueTemple.desc: Temple meditation in the mountain mist: climb worn steps through the rain to a guided candle meditation among stone Buddhas. 19 minutes, free, offline.
antiqueTemple.h1: The Ancient Temple: an immersive Buddhist temple meditation

cosmicTemple.seo: Cosmic Meditation: Guided Journey with a Celestial Whale
cosmicTemple.desc: Cosmic meditation for a taste of higher consciousness: a guided journey on a celestial whale to a marble temple where a star is born. 13 minutes, free.
cosmicTemple.h1: The Cosmic Temple: an immersive cosmic meditation

crystalCave.seo: Crystal Cave Meditation for Clarity: A Free Guided Journey
crystalCave.desc: Crystal cave meditation deep underground: follow a butterfly past glowing crystals and mirror-still pools. A 17-minute clarity meditation, free, no ads.
crystalCave.h1: The Infinite Crystal Cave: an immersive crystal meditation
crystalCave.lead: This crystal cave meditation begins with a crack in the rock, opening onto a cavern of glowing crystals. In this guided visualization, a crystal-winged butterfly shows you the way. A singing mermaid, a sleepy little dragon and a tiny glowing city wait deeper inside. At heart, this is a clarity meditation: the crystal light can carry away what weighs on you.

galaxy.desc: Space meditation: board a silent train of light past Saturn's icy rings and a shower of shooting stars. A guided galaxy meditation, 19 minutes, free, offline.
galaxy.h1: Journey Through the Galaxy: an immersive space meditation
galaxy.lead: This space meditation takes you aboard a silent train of light, through Saturn's icy rings and shooting stars. It stops at a night market on an asteroid. earthCore.seo: Guided Grounding Meditation: Journey to the Earth's Core
earthCore.desc: Guided grounding meditation: descend through crystal caverns and rivers of warm light to the heart of the planet. An earth meditation, 15 minutes, free.
earthCore.h1: The Heart of the Earth: an immersive grounding meditation
earthCore.lead: This grounding meditation follows warm rivers of light deep underground. They lead to a hollow land with a gentle sun of its own. antarcticBase.seo: Winter Meditation: A Silent Frozen Sanctuary Under the Ice

antarcticBase.h1: The Frozen Sanctuary: an immersive guided winter meditation
antarcticBase.lead: In this winter meditation, you sink through ancient layers of ice to a sanctuary older than memory. A glowing polar fox shows you the way. skyIsland.seo: Safe Place Visualization: Floating Island Meditation, Free
skyIsland.desc: A safe place visualization and island meditation: rest on your own floating island above the clouds, beside a winged white stag. 19 minutes, free, offline.
skyIsland.h1: The Floating Island: a safe place visualization
skyIsland.lead: This safe place visualization begins on a bridge of clouds, leading to a green island that is yours alone. Ride a great white bird and meet the winged stag who guards it. zenGarden.seo: Zen Meditation: A Guided Zen Garden Meditation, Koi and Tea
zenGarden.desc: Zen meditation in a Japanese garden: walk slow stone paths under cherry blossoms, past koi and raked sand. A guided zen garden meditation, 18 minutes, free.
zenGarden.h1: The Zen Garden: a guided zen meditation in a Japanese garden
zenGarden.lead: This zen meditation, guided step by step, takes you into a quiet Japanese garden still fresh from the rain. A cherry tree bursts into bloom and koi glide under a wooden bridge. An old gardener shares his tea, and stone lanterns light your way back at dusk. Rather than a lesson, this zen garden meditation is a slow walk: you only need to follow the path.

atlantis.seo: Underwater Meditation in Atlantis: Guided Ocean Meditation
atlantis.desc: Underwater meditation in Atlantis: breathe freely, ride a golden seahorse through a lost city of coral. A guided ocean meditation, 17 minutes, free, offline.
atlantis.h1: Underwater Atlantis: an immersive underwater meditation

himalayanMonastery.seo: Mountain Meditation: Himalayan Monastery at Sunrise, Free
himalayanMonastery.desc: Mountain meditation at sunrise: snowy Himalayan peaks, prayer flags in the cold wind, the first golden light. A free morning meditation, 18 minutes, no ads.
himalayanMonastery.h1: Monastery at Sunrise: a Himalayan mountain meditation
himalayanMonastery.lead: This mountain meditation begins at a monastery before dawn, where an old monk lights the way with a butter lamp. celestialLibrary.seo: Akashic Library Meditation: Flying Books Beneath the Stars
celestialLibrary.desc: A guided Akashic library meditation: wander among glowing books and spiral staircases beneath moving constellations. 13 minutes, free, no ads, offline.
celestialLibrary.h1: The Celestial Library: an Akashic library meditation
celestialLibrary.lead: Step through a great wooden door into an Akashic library lit by floating candles. Here, books glide down to any reader who raises a hand. In this gentle Akashic meditation, a salamander of golden light keeps you company as two books open for you.

desertOasis.desc: Oasis meditation by moonlight: a guided desert meditation that leads you to glowing water under an immense moon and a sky full of stars. 13 minutes, free.
desertOasis.h1: The Desert Oasis: an immersive oasis meditation
desertOasis.lead: This oasis meditation starts on the dunes at sunset. Ride a white camel beside a spirit of golden sand. At the oasis, a night market and a lamp full of butterflies are waiting, and a garden lies hidden beneath the pool. This desert meditation ends by a small fire, under an immense moon.

treeOfConsciousness.seo: Tree of Life Meditation: A Guided Tree Visualization, Free
treeOfConsciousness.desc: Tree of life meditation in a glowing night forest: a guided tree visualization, from shining roots to branches that hold the stars. 18 minutes, free, offline.
treeOfConsciousness.h1: The Tree of Consciousness: a tree of life meditation
treeOfConsciousness.lead: This tree of life meditation leads you through a forest that glows in the dark. At its heart stands a vast world tree joining the earth and the stars. Its guardian of wood and moss lets you feel every life beating. Then a single leaf opens onto a gentle little world. This is a tree visualization from the roots up: you climb, look out over the forest, then come back to sit against the trunk.

jungleRuins.seo: Jungle Meditation: Guided Rainforest Journey to a Lost City
jungleRuins.desc: Jungle meditation in a lost city: explore an overgrown temple where waterfalls pour over old stone. A guided rainforest meditation, 18 minutes, free, offline.
jungleRuins.h1: The Forgotten Ruins: an immersive jungle meditation
jungleRuins.lead: This jungle meditation begins as the mist lifts from a city lost beneath the trees. A little monkey of light leads you through its ruins. You dive to an older city under the water and see a tree spring from the seed you plant. From the first step, this rainforest meditation is warm, green and unhurried.

mushroomForest.desc: Enchanted forest meditation in a dreamlike wood of giant glowing mushrooms and butterflies of light. A guided forest visualization, 17 minutes, free, no ads.
mushroomForest.h1: The Dream Forest: an immersive enchanted forest meditation
mushroomForest.lead: This enchanted forest meditation feels like stepping inside a dream, among giant mushrooms that glow like blue lamps. Pick a tiny galaxy from a silver tree, follow butterflies of light and float above it all on a gentle octopus. This forest visualization asks for nothing but curiosity.

mirrorDimension.seo: Self-Awareness Meditation: A Guided Mirror Meditation, Free
mirrorDimension.desc: Self-awareness meditation among endless mirrors and soft white light: rest as the calm witness. A guided mirror meditation, 16 minutes, free, offline.
mirrorDimension.h1: The Mirror Dimension: an immersive self-awareness meditation
mirrorDimension.lead: This self-awareness meditation lets you drift weightless through white light and countless mirrors. One of them shows an animal guide instead of your face. Together you pass through small dreamlike worlds, then come back to the quiet awareness behind every reflection. It is a mirror meditation with one question at its heart: who is looking?

wolfForest.seo: Wolf Spirit Animal Meditation Under the Northern Lights
wolfForest.desc: Meet your wolf spirit animal: walk a snowy pine forest under the northern lights with a gentle pack. A guided wolf meditation, 15 minutes, free, no ads.
wolfForest.h1: The Wolf Spirit Forest: meet your wolf spirit animal
wolfForest.lead: Step into a moonlit pine forest, where your wolf spirit animal, made of stars, leads you to its pack. Run with them until you become a wolf yourself, howl at an enormous moon and cross a bridge of northern lights. This wolf meditation ends by a small fire, with your wolf sitting beside you.

sections.h2: How to share it with your team
sections.p: There is nothing to install on your side and nothing to roll out. Share the download link in your newsletter, on your intranet or in a team channel, and each person installs the app on their own phone. Since there are no accounts, there is no user list to manage and no access to revoke. It is not a corporate meditation program with a teacher and a schedule: each person simply opens the app when they choose.
bullets: Share the App Store and Google Play links
Suggest a first session, such as one from the 4 Minutes category
Let everyone use it freely and privately

faq: Is it really free for companies?
Yes. The app is free for everyone, with no subscription, no ads and no paid business version. Your team can use every session without any cost.
What data does the app collect about employees?
None. There is no account, and the app collects no personal data. Each person's practice history stays on their own phone, so the employer has no access to it.
Do we need to set anything up?
No. There is no deployment, admin panel or license to manage. You simply share the download link, and each colleague installs the app on their iPhone or Android phone.
How do you meditate at work?

To meditate at work, keep it short and simple. Sit back in your chair, put on headphones and play a session of about four minutes between two tasks. If closing your eyes feels awkward in an open office, lower your gaze instead.
